questions.question: Discuss the structure and function of thoracic appendages in prawns. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Discuss the structure and function of thoracic appendages in prawns. [U]/[CO2]
  • Thoracic appendages in prawns include three pairs of maxillipeds and five pairs of
  • pereiopods (walking legs). All are biramous, and have protopodite of two podomeres and endopodite
  • of 5 podomeres an d an unsegmented exopodite. Coxa of first 3 thoracic appendages bears epipodite,
  • which is used for respiration. Second maxilliped curved like a question mark. First 3 pairs of walking
  • legs are chelate type and last two are non -chelate type. Maxillipeds are used for Handling and
  • manipulation of food. Pereiopods have walking, grasping, and reproductive or cleaning roles.
  • (Diagram not necessary, If diagram of all thoracic appendages drawn,give full mark)

  • sea cucumbers (bioturbation) improve the oxygenation and permeability of seafloor substrates.
  • Economic importance- Holothuroidea have been harvested for centuries and are used for producing
  • high-value seafood delicacyand medicinal products. (Liberal valuation).

questions.question: Explain the circulatory system in Prawn. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the circulatory system in prawn. [U]/[CO2]
  • The prawn has an open circulatory system. The blood vascular system consists of heart, pericardium,
  • arteries, blood lacunae, and haemolymph (haemocyanin ). The heart pumps the blood into arteries,
  • which branch out into the body cavity, allowing the blood to bathe the organs directly. From there, the
  • blood returns to the heart via a series of channels and sinuses after passing through the gills to pick up
  • oxygen. Blood carried to gills by afferent branchial channels. Pure blood after oxygenation is carried
  • to the pericardial sinus by efferent branchial channels. From there blood flows to heart through ostia.
